newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-DORTMUND POWER TO 3-1 WIN OVER AUXERRE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-DORTMUND POWER TO 3-1 WIN OVER AUXERRE.

text.p: Goals by Karlheinz Riedle, Rene Schneider and Andy Moeller gave Borussia Dortmund a 3-1 first-leg advantage in their European Cup quarter-final against Auxerre.

The German champions, 2-0 up with 15 minutes to go, had to step up a gear after French international midfielder Sabri Lamouchi capitalised on some slack defending to make it 2-1 -- a scoreline Auxerre would have been happy to take back to France.
Dortmund coach Ottmar Hitzfeld responded by bringing on Ibrahim Tanko in the 80th minute. Two minutes later, the Ghanaian striker set up Moeller, who produced a lethal finish to make it 3-1.
"We can live with this result," Hitzfeld said. "We have a good chance now of reaching the semifinal. We're good enough away from home to score two or three goals."
Riedle established Dortmund's lead in the 12th minute with a close-range header.
The goal followed a fine build-up from Joerg Heinrich and Swiss international striker Stephane Chapuisat, who produced a stunning overhead kick to get the ball to Riedle.

Schneider, who replaced injured libero Wolfgang Feiersinger late in the first half, put Dortmund 2-0 ahead in the 54th minute. His powerful header flew past Lionel Charbonnier after an inch-perfect free-kick from Chapuisat.
But Dortmund, missing first-choice defenders Julio Cesar, Juergen Kohler and Matthias Sammer because of injury, always looked vulnerable at the back and Lamouchi took full advantage.
"Lamouchi's goal gives us some hope," Auxerre coach Guy Roux said, expressing delight that his side had shrugged off their recent poor league form to take the game to Dortmund.
"If we'd played as we have in the league recently, we'd have gone down by eight goals here."
Stefan Reuter, who deputised for suspended captain Michael Zorc, will miss the return leg after being sent off late in the game for a second bookable offence.

"The result is a bit dangerous but I'm optimistic," Reuter said. "You've got to hand it to Rene Schneider. He's come straight into a game like this after a lot of injuries and bad luck and he's scored a goal."
Spanish referee Josia Maria Garcia-Aranda had both sets of supporters in the 47,500-strong crowd howling after refusing each side a goal in the first half.
Chapuisat was ruled to have handled the ball on its way into the net in the seventh minute and a spectacular overhead shot from Auxerre's Lilian Laslandes was disallowed for dangerous play.

"I've looked at 10 television replays of that goal and I think the referee made the wrong decision," Roux said of the Laslandes effort. "It wasn't dangerous play because the Dortmund defender next to him was far enough away."
